# Layouts by path: JSON, MessagePack and ROS 2

A stream whose messages are JSON, MessagePack or ROS 2 messages
declares, in `streams.toml`, a decoder of `kind = "json"`,
`kind = "msgpack"` or `kind = "cdr"` whose fields each give a
`path` through the message (see
[Configuration](../concepts/configuration.md)). Every recording stores
the layout, so the recording can be decoded without the configuration
it was made with.

```toml
[streams.arm.decoder]
kind = "json"

[[streams.arm.decoder.fields]]
name = "joint_positions"
type = "f64"
path = "joints.position"
count = 7
unit = "rad"
```

## Paths

A path is keys separated by dots, with `[n]` for the n-th element of an
array, counted from 0: `joints.position[2]`, `state.pose.x`, `[0].id`.
A key is any text without `.`, `[` or `]`; in MessagePack, a key that
is a number matches its digits. A field with `count` above 1 names an
array and takes its first `count` elements.

An element can also be found by name: `position[name=shoulder]` is
the element of `position` at the place where the array `name` beside
it holds `shoulder`, as a ROS 2 `JointState` lists its joints. The
field is then the same joint whatever order the robot sends its
joints in; a message without the name is missing the field, never
given another joint's value. A path looks up one name, for one value
(`count` 1): declare a field for each joint. Each such field reads
the message twice, once to find the name and once for the value.

## Values

Each value is converted to the field's `type` by the same rules in
every format, then multiplied by its `scale` if it has one:

| Type | Accepts |
|---|---|
| `u8` … `u64`, `i8` … `i64` | integers in the type's range; numbers without a fraction (`3.0`), in range; `true` as 1 and `false` as 0 |
| `f32`, `f64` | any number, an `f32` rounded to 32 bits; `true` as 1 and `false` as 0 |
| `bool` | `true` and `false`; numbers: 0 is false, anything else true |

A path that isn't in the message, or a name it doesn't hold, leaves
that field missing and the others decoded: a topic two publishers
share, such as an arm's and a gripper's joint states, gives each
field from the messages that have it. The live view and the replay
keep a missing value's last one, the quality checks have no value for
it at that time, and `kapto decode` leaves its cell empty; it is never
read as 0. A message with none of its fields isn't decoded.

Text, `null`, maps and arrays where a value is expected, or a value
outside its type's range, leave the message undecoded; it is still
recorded exactly as it arrived. So is a message that isn't valid JSON
or MessagePack.

## In a recording

The stream's MCAP channel has message encoding `kapto.json/v1` or
`kapto.msgpack/v1`: each message is the payload exactly as received.
The channel's schema has the same encoding, the stream's name as its
name, and the layout as JSON as its data:

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "sequence",
      "type": "u32",
      "path": "header.seq",
      "count": 1,
      "scale": null,
      "unit": null
    },
    {
      "name": "joint_positions",
      "type": "f64",
      "path": "joints.position",
      "count": 7,
      "scale": null,
      "unit": "rad"
    }
  ]
}
```

Every key is always written. A reader requires `name`, `type` and
`path`; `count` defaults to 1, and `scale` and `unit` to none. The
keys mean the same as in a [struct layout](struct-layout.md), with
`path` in place of `offset` and `byte_order`.

## ROS 2 messages

A stream of ROS 2 messages, serialised as ROS 2 does (CDR), names
their type too, and finds fields by path through the message as its
definition lays it out: `header.stamp.sec`, `position[2]`.

```toml
[streams.joints.decoder]
kind = "cdr"
type = "sensor_msgs/msg/JointState"

[[streams.joints.decoder.fields]]
name = "position"
type = "f64"
path = "position"
count = 7
unit = "rad"
```

The type's definition is put together from `.msg` files in the `msg/`
folder beside `streams.toml`, laid out as ROS 2 installs them: the
type's own, `msg/sensor_msgs/msg/JointState.msg`, and that of every
type it uses (`msg/std_msgs/msg/Header.msg`,
`msg/builtin_interfaces/msg/Time.msg`), copied from a ROS 2
installation's `share` folder. A file not in the package is looked
for in the ROS 2 installation Kapto runs in, in each `share` folder of
`AMENT_PREFIX_PATH` in turn. A missing file is
`decoder.msg_not_found`, naming it and the type that uses it. A
recording carries every `.msg` file its streams use, at the same place
beside `streams.toml`: the package's among its files, and those read
from the installation besides, so it reads back without either.

A ROS 2 topic (`ros2 = { topic, type }`) is decoded the same way;
its decoder has the topic's `type`, and needs none of its own.

In a recording the stream is stored as rosbag2 stores a topic, so
ROS 2's tools and Foxglove read it: message encoding
`cdr`, and a schema of encoding `ros2msg` named
after the type (`sensor_msgs/msg/JointState`) whose data is its
definition as rosbag2 writes it: the type's own `.msg` file, then each
type it uses, once, depth first, each type's in alphabetical order,
after a line of 80 `=` and `MSG: package/Type`. Kapto's fields go in
the channel's metadata under `kapto.fields`, as the JSON above. A
channel of this encoding without them, recorded by another tool,
decodes into no values.

A topic is stored the same way, with or without a decoder. Its
channel is named after the stream, as every channel is, and the topic
it was received on is in the channel's metadata under
`ros2.topic`. `ros2 bag info` and Foxglove read the recording;
rosbag2 doesn't replay or convert it, as it refuses a bag whose
channels have more than one encoding, and Kapto's own events channel
is JSON. `kapto export rosbag2` writes an episode's topics as a bag of
their own (one MCAP file, profile `ros2`): each channel named after
its topic, with its schema, and each message with its sequence and
both times as recorded, which `ros2 bag play` replays.
